baseline_sources.qualifications: GT-F34 (CSPH margin clock- and density-dependent, post hoc) and GT-F35 (E0 rare-mass numerical artefacts) qualify the published N<=6 values; comparisons use the in-round gtobs re-derivations, and the published values are checked against them on robust channels only (Z4)

chosen_because: GT-P003 pre-freeze review (gravity-time/reports/gt-e1-prefreeze-review.md; gravity-time/docs/e1-design-alternatives.md option B, head 31620b6f6d0ccb1d381a95803c7552d506ae96e3), authorised by the human researcher in GT-P004

clocks.continuous: pi_ct = pi_jump / R (event weights as rates); per-unit-time observables
clocks.event_order: consecutive event pairs on the stationary jump chain
clocks.jump: pi_jump, the stationary law of the embedded jump chain; per-event observables

comparisons.C1_native_size_sequence: every declared channel at HELD W4 for N=5, 6 (in-round gtobs re-derivations of published cells) and N=7, per family
comparisons.C2_strength_response: W4 -> W3 -> W16 at N=5 and N=6 for each non-gradient family; per channel, the three values and whether they are monotone in log-strength (a step below the negligible floor counts as consistent); monotonicity is not presumed

C3_calibration.classes: both_negligible | size_step_negligible | strength_step_negligible | opposite | same_sign_comparable_size (strength/size step ratio in [0.5, 2]) | same_sign_different_size | unavailable
C3_calibration.contrast: N=5 W16 (every log-factor x2, matching the path-witness maximum 12 -> 24) against N=6 W4, both relative to N=5 W4, per declared channel
C3_calibration.family_verdict: among channels whose size step is non-negligible and strength step available: usable_proxy if >= 0.667 are same_sign_comparable_size; direction_only_proxy if >= 0.667 share the sign; otherwise poor_proxy
C3_calibration.reading_rule: a poor_proxy family's N=7 strength readings are reported but not used as evidence for or against witness amplification; matching the witness maximum does not match engaged loads, state-space combinatorics or transition laws

C4_n7_against_strength_response.classes: size_step_negligible | no_strength_response | strength_response_non_monotone | opposite_to_strength_response | same_sign_within_bracket_range ([0.5 x smallest, 2 x largest] non-negligible response) | same_sign_outside_bracket_range | unavailable
C4_n7_against_strength_response.contrast: N=6 -> N=7 step at W4 against the W3 and W16 responses at N=6 (the path-witness maximum ratio 40/24 = 1.667 lies between log-strength 1.585 and 2)

comparisons.C5_component_engagement: per component, event share, mean engaged witnesses and mean engaged log-weight on the jump chain (gtobs witness census) at every cell; N7/N6 mean log-weight ratio placed below W3 (1.585), within W3-W16, or above W16 (2)
comparisons.C6_geometric_reference: null attachment fraction r0, source share 3/N and NULL hub rates at N=5, 6, 7, reported beside every margin; neither is separately identified by the N sequence
comparisons.C7_clock_and_density: every margin in four forms (raw, ceiling-normalised (af-r0)/(1-r0), null-density-standardised, full a/k profile) in both clocks, side by side; none is primary. The standardised margin is a counterfactual reweighting to the NULL law's free-edge-count distribution and may weight free-edge counts that are rare under the cell's own law; rare-mass flags mark such conditionals
comparisons.no_aggregate_score: profiles are reported per channel; no weighted score is formed

controls_and_structural_expectations.Z1_null_identity: NULL at N=5, 6, 7: pi uniform (class-level L1 <= 1e-09), irreversible flux <= 1e-09, raw and standardised margins |.| <= 1e-09 in both clocks (theorem; N=7 previously evaluated as a fixture)
controls_and_structural_expectations.Z2_gradient_control: CLOSEW at N=5, 6, 7 (W4): predicted triple-Gibbs law (L1 <= 1e-09) and irreversible flux <= 1e-09
controls_and_structural_expectations.Z3_non_gradient_rates: every non-gradient cell (all sizes and alphabets): maximum square affinity > 1e-06. A rate property of the rules; stationary flux is not predicted (E0A X4 saturation)
controls_and_structural_expectations.Z4_baseline_replication: each N=5, 6 W4 re-derivation agrees with its published E0B cell on ['held_continuous/attachment_fraction', 'held_jump/attachment_fraction', 'reversibility/irreversible_flux_fraction', 'reversibility/entropy_production_per_event', 'event_order/pattern_asymmetry', 'occupancy_ct/expected_edges', 'hub_frame/event_order/pattern_asymmetry'] within max(1e-10, 1e-08 x |published|). Rare-mass channels qualified by GT-F35 are excluded by declaration
controls_and_structural_expectations.Z5_numerical_acceptance: per cell: stationary resolved (residual <= 1e-12; two starts within 1e-10 L1; iteration cap not reached), symmetry <= 1e-10, autocorrelation cap not reached, kernel sample check, no zero-mass reachable state, per-entry long-double residual, referee agreement (tolerances below). A tally, not a prediction: a failed cell is reported as unresolved or numerically qualified, never as a scientific counterexample, and never re-run with weaker tolerances
controls_and_structural_expectations.Z6_hub_frame_reversible_controls: NULL and CLOSEW cells: hub-frame pattern asymmetry and hub-frame net current <= 1e-09
controls_and_structural_expectations.separation_note: Z1-Z6 are identities, rule properties and numerical acceptance. None predicts the sign or size of any margin, flux, handover index or strength response

deliberate_omissions.free_n7: FREE N=7 (option D) is not authorised in GT-P004; preserved as a separate future decision
deliberate_omissions.grade_or_alphabet_sweeps: no further grades, alphabets, interpolations or sizes
deliberate_omissions.pcomp: PCOMP (E0B rules-vs-ratio control) is not part of option B
deliberate_omissions.recurrent_class_list: reducible classes are not decomposed beyond [size] (gtobs)
deliberate_omissions.spectrum: the generator spectrum is unavailable at every N in this round: gtobs never forms the dense generator (GT-P003). Reported as unavailable, not zero; published N<=6 spectra are not compared

estimands: the declared channels and every gtobs channel of each cell, the comparisons C1-C8, and the controls Z1-Z6
initial_conditions: as E0: the HELD start state gt0.start_state(n, 'HELD'), the source triangle {0,1,2} present and no other relation; source slots are present and cannot dissolve; the reachable class from that start is analysed

numerical_policy.autocorrelation: gtobs lazy Poisson series to relative term 1e-13, cap 2000000
numerical_policy.gth_referee: where the class has at most 4096 states (N=5, 6): the Grassmann-Taksar-Heyman dense solve (subtraction-free) with the same tolerances
numerical_policy.kernel_sample_check: the family's rule strings and scaffold, parsed by the laboratory DSL and evaluated with exact Fraction factors on 400 seeded states plus the start and the fullest state (seed sha256('round-e1:kernel:<item_id>')[:16]); gtkernel weights within relative 1e-12, identical zero pattern, correct targets. W3/W16 are float in gtkernel and exact in the DSL, so the comparison is by tolerance
numerical_policy.long_double_residual: per-entry relative residual |(pi P)_i - pi_i| / pi_i in numpy longdouble <= 1e-09; zero-mass reachable states must be 0 (guards against the GT-F35 clipping)
numerical_policy.rare_conditionals: any conditional channel whose conditioning mass is < 1e-12 is flagged rare and not interpreted; < 1e-06 is flagged low. Values are kept, never clipped
numerical_policy.stationary: gtobs.stationary: lazy power iteration by gathers from the uniform law until L1 change < 1e-15 and per-entry relative change < 1e-13; second run from the point mass on the start must agree within 1e-10 L1; residual <= 1e-12; cap 2000000 iterations; no dense solve, no clipping of positive mass
numerical_policy.symmetry: class tables over the HELD symmetry group (S3 on the source x S(N-3) on the probes); max orbit disagreement <= 1e-10
numerical_policy.third_start: a third run from the point mass on the reachable state with the most relations; law L1 <= 1e-10, per-entry relative <= 1e-08, headline channels within 1e-10
numerical_policy.threads: children run with single-threaded BLAS/OpenMP; results reproducible to about 1e-15, not bitwise

observables.gtobs: every channel of rs_constraint_lab.gtobs.analyse (gt-e1-observables/v1): occupancy, held observables in both clocks (attachment, a/k profile, distance distribution, radial drift, escape and capture), shell activity in both clocks, reversibility (flux, entropy production, square affinities), projected currents, class-free and hub-frame event order, class tables, Gibbs projection, autocorrelation times, e1 additions (standardised margin, detached-probe counts, hub structure, engaged witness census, hub persistence)
observables.round: handover index: the four steps of the E0 handover cycle (FPFA, FADP, DPDA, DAFP), forward minus reverse probability, adjacent and disjoint, and the count of forward-oriented adjacent steps
observables.trajectories: illustrative only, 4 x 400 events per cell, seeds sha256('round-e1:<item_id>:<k>')[:16]; no table statistic uses them

open_questions_without_prediction: GT-Q07: at N=7, is CSPH's attachment margin above or below the size-specific null, in each clock and each form, and does it coexist with irreversible flux?
Does the handover keep the E0 orientation at N=7 in every non-gradient family, reverse, or vanish?
Does the equal-ratio occupancy gap keep growing at N=7, and under strengthening?
How does shell structure (shells 1-4, activity in both clocks) change at N=7?
How much does the engaged witness load grow from N=6 to N=7, per component, and where does it sit against the W3/W16 bracket?
Does the W3/W16 bracket reproduce the published N=5 -> N=6 step (calibration), especially for PATHF and PATHH?
Is any N=6 -> N=7 change in the direction of strengthening at N=6, opposite to it, or outside its range?
Do hub structure and the hub-frame arrow change with N beyond the changing null hub rates?

pre_freeze_exposure.bracket_kernel_builds: tests/test_gtobs.py builds HELD N=5 W3 and W16 kernels of CSPH, PATHF and CLOSEW and compares weights and targets with build_kernel; no stationary law or observable was computed. No other W3/W16 cell of these families was computed
pre_freeze_exposure.engineering_after_gt_p003: before freezing, gte1 was exercised only on synthetic N=4 cells (W4, W3, W16), on published N=5 and N=6 W4 cells (baseline items: CSPH, PATHH, NULL, CLOSEW at N=5; CSPH at N=6, for timing), and on the theorem-fixed HELD N=7 CLOSE strong_favour fixture (not a round cell; costs and solver checks only). The HELD N=5 W16 PATHF kernel was rebuilt by a test (weights only). No N=7 round cell and no W3/W16 stationary law at N=5 or 6 was computed
pre_freeze_exposure.gt_p003_reproduction: all 84 published E0 cells were recomputed by gtobs in GT-P003 (validation log); this includes every N=5, 6 W4 baseline of this round
pre_freeze_exposure.n7_fixtures: three N=7 cost fixtures were run in GT-P003: HELD NULL (identity; this round's N=7 NULL cell is therefore exposed), HELD CLOSE strong_favour (not a round cell), FREE NULL (not a round cell). The GT-P003 design draft listed FREE CLOSE as exposed; it was never run
pre_freeze_exposure.n7_kernel_build: the HELD N=7 PATHF weak_suppress chain was built for timing in the E1 kernel step (4dacd11); no stationary law or observable was computed
pre_freeze_exposure.post_hoc_channels: engaged witness census, margin decomposition (raw, standardised, jump/continuous) and hub structure on published N=5, 6 cells (reports/e1-engaged-witness-n5-n6.json, reports/e1-margin-decomposition-n5-n6.json); GT-F34 is post hoc
pre_freeze_exposure.published_n_le_6: all E0A and E0B tables (N=5, 6, W4) were read in full; the 16 baseline items re-derive published cells and are not new observations
pre_freeze_exposure.theorem_fixed: NULL baselines at N=5, 6, 7 (uniform law) and the scale census (reports/e1-scale-census.json)

question: How do occupancy, kinetics, stationary circulation (the handover) and source-relative attachment reorganise from N=5, 6 to N=7 at fixed grades, and how much of that change resembles what uniform strengthening of the same rules does at fixed N?
sampling: exact census of 32 authorised cells (tranche I: 8; tranche II: 24) plus 16 baseline re-derivations

stop_conditions.amendment: a solver-only correction after freeze keeps this plan, is documented with its effect and validated independently, and marks affected results; any change to cells or estimands stops the round for explicit amendment
stop_conditions.item: each cell runs in its own process; past its watchdog ({5: 900, 6: 900, 7: 3600} seconds by N) it is killed and recorded unresolved_watchdog, or complete_checks_interrupted if its main result was already written; the round continues
stop_conditions.round: all items have final records, or the 14400-second wall cap from the first launch: running cells are recorded interrupted_wall_cap, unstarted cells not_started_wall_cap, and the round stops
stop_conditions.stop_rule_reading: per GT-P004 section 5 (matching the GT-P003 roadmap proposal): a margin crossing below null is an observation for that family, N, clock and definition; it does not by itself establish a finite-size effect, amplification or a failure of the ontology; grades are not retuned
stop_conditions.unresolved: an unresolved stationary law is recorded without stationary observables; no post-freeze retuning of tolerances, grades, alphabets, cells or channels

work_count.estimate_note: measured on this host before freezing (16 cores, about 8 GB available): the full gte1 cell pipeline on the theorem-fixed HELD N=7 CLOSE strong_favour fixture took 156 s (main 126 s, checks 31 s) at 590 MB peak; on the published HELD N=6 W4 CSPH baseline 43 s (GTH referee 42 s) at 300 MB; N=5 under 1 s. Scientific N=7 cells are extrapolated at 3-6 min (stationary iterations 300-1,100 against the fixture's 537). Round: about 40-65 cell-minutes, 15-30 min wall with 4 workers. Estimates, not guarantees
